claims.text: Cr preferentially segregates to and oxidizes at the surfaces of CrFeCoNiX alloys during exposure above 900 °C.
Combining Cr with Al or Si promotes formation of a thin protective oxide layer.
The oxide layers formed on the Al- or Si-containing alloys are coherent and adherent.
The protective oxide on the Al- or Si-containing alloys persists in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres above 900 °C.
Using Mn as X fails to provide the oxide–substrate lattice matching needed for protection.
The Mn-containing alloy forms a thicker, non-coherent oxide.
The oxide formed on the Mn-containing alloy cracks or spalls.
Lattice matching of Cr-, Al-, or Si-rich oxides with the alloy substrate facilitates a coherent oxide–substrate interface.
Preferential oxidation and surface segregation of Cr together with Al or Si produces a stable, adherent oxide.
The stable oxide produced by Cr together with Al or Si minimizes interfacial stress.
Insufficient lattice compatibility of the Mn-associated oxide causes stress accumulation.
Stress accumulation in the Mn-associated oxide leads to cracking and spallation.
Cracking and spallation of the Mn-associated oxide accelerate surface degradation.
The proposed behavior applies to CrFeCoNiX alloys in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states above 900 °C.
The proposed behavior may not apply to substantially different alloy compositions or microstructures.
